title.narrative: Provision of live-saving FSL assistance to most vulnerable communities in Qansaxdheere district, Bay region, SWS, Somalia to address impacts of dry conditions and mitigate displacement

description.narrative: ltpgtSomalia is experiencing a severe and prolonged humanitarian crisis in 2025, fueled by consecutive climatic shocks, widespread displacement, insecurity, and weak service delivery systems. The latest IPC analysis (April–June 2025) estimates that 4.6 million people—almost one in four Somalis—are facing acute food insecurity at Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or Emergency (IPC Phase 4) levels. Additionally, 1.8 million children under five are acutely malnourished, including 479,000 with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM). The failure of successive Gu and Deyr rainy seasons, rising food prices, displacement of over 3 million people, and reduced access to humanitarian aid have worsened the crisis. Malnutrition is being driven by poor feeding practices, high disease prevalence, and limited WASH and health services (IPC).ltbrgtThe Bay Region has been among the worst affected areas. Drought, crop failure, livestock loss, and water scarcity have caused staple food production to drop by more than 60% below the five-year average. Agropastoral households, who depend on rain-fed farming and livestock, have seen their food access and income drastically reduced. GAM rates have exceeded the WHO emergency threshold of 15% in many areas, disproportionately affecting children under five, pregnant and lactating women, and displaced families. Insecurity and logistical barriers have restricted access to health and nutrition services (IPC analysis April-June 2025).ltbrgtQansaxdheere District is facing particularly alarming conditions. Recurrent droughts and erratic rainfall have led to massive crop failure, loss of livestock, and widespread food and water insecurity. Based on IPC report of March 2025 Most households is classified as IPC Phase 3 (Crisis), with 7% of population in Phase 4 (Emergency). Families are resorting to negative coping mechanisms such as selling remaining assets, reducing meals, withdrawing children from school, or engaging in harmful survival strategies like charcoal production. Recent assessments reveal GAM rates above 17% and SAM levels at or above 3%, surpassing emergency thresholds (IPC analysis April-June 2025).ltbrgtContributing factors to this acute crisis include limited dietary diversity, diarrheal diseases, inadequate infant feeding practices, and severely constrained access to nutrition and WASH services. The scarcity of therapeutic feeding programs and inadequate infrastructure further deepen vulnerabilities (IPC). lt/pgtltpgtThe project intervention includes: Unconditional Cash Transfers (UCT): 240 elderly, disabled and marginalized households will receive monthly cash for three months to meet urgent needs. The UCT will target 420 disabled beneficiariesltbrgtConditional Cash Transfers (CCT): 960 households will participate in CfW activities focused on the rehabilitation of community catchments over a three-month period. lt/pgtltpgtWater Infrastructure Rehabilitation: The restoration of 5 pans will address both immediate income needs and long-term water security, supporting agriculture, livestock, and domestic water use while reducing distress migration and environmental degradation.ltbrgtTraining of WMC: Committees will be trained in sustainable water management, governance, conflict resolution, and inclusivity to ensure ownership and sustainability of water infrastructure.ltbrgtMobile money will be used for cash distribution, offering a secure, fast, and cost-effective method that empowers households to prioritize their own needs and strengthens local markets. This approach offers an effective solution to both immediate humanitarian needs and longer-term resilience building. It will directly support food and nutrition security, protect livelihoods, enhance water access, and build the capacity to cope with future shocks. The total target population includes 2,376 women, 2,016 men, 1,512 girls, 1,296 boys across 4 villages and 4 IDP camps.ltbrgtlt/pgt
